title: Théorie arithmétique. Théorie de Galois des motifs (1965) : notes manuscites (s.d.), tapuscrit (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: these are 1965 notes on the 'Galois theory of motives', written on the back of a Bourbaki typescript (Tribu 59, Lie algebras). Grothendieck considers a motive (or family of motives) over a base scheme X, presumably of characteristic p or arithmetic. He compares two kinds of 'fibre' or realization data: the l-adic one (xi_l) and the p-adic one (xi_p, xi*_p).

(1) l-adic. The l-adic realizations xi_l at a point x of X depend on the choice of a geometric point of X. They are well defined only up to isomorphism, through the transport isomorphisms of the fundamental groupoid. pi_1(X) acts on xi_l, so the system is a local system on X, i.e. a representation of pi_1(X). Up to this unique-up-to-pi_1 ambiguity, the fibre is independent of the choice.

(2) p-adic. The p-adic realization xi*_p behaves differently. It depends on a point of X with values in a perfect field V and nothing more. Equivalently one may use the perfect closure k(x)^parf of the residue field k(x). The fibre at such a point is a module over the Witt vectors W_p(k) ('partie entière', i.e. the integral W(k)-lattice). For a fixed perfect field k one gets a system of isomorphisms between the xi^{(x)}_{p,a} attached to the various k-valued points lying over the same x ∈ X. Automorphisms of k act on W_p(k) (itérés de Frobenius) and hence semilinearly.

The key contrast is stated explicitly. pi_1(X) no longer acts on xi*_p. Instead, the group of automorphisms of k over k(x) acts on the localized fibre xi^{(x)}_p, semilinearly. In return there is an extra structure: the operators F and V with FV = p. This is Dieudonné-module or F-crystal structure. The scribbled remarks about 'conjugates' and the bottom-left note 'il faut mettre deux conjugués' seem to deal with Frobenius-conjugate (twisted) fibres: for a perfect field, the Frobenius-twisted point gives a conjugate fibre, and one must keep track of this in the notation.

Notation fixed at the end:
- (i) xi_{x̄,l} for a geometric point; xi_{x,l} for a point with values in an arbitrary field, defined up to isomorphism (unique up to the Galois action).
- (ii) xi_{x,p} for a point with values in a perfect field, and a variant xi°_{x,p}, probably the integral lattice or the version without extra structure.

Purpose: to set up the 'fibre functors' of a motivic Galois theory over a base. The l-adic fibre functors form a pi_1-torsor-like groupoid. The p-adic (Dieudonné/crystalline) fibre functors are semilinear objects over W(k), with Frobenius, functorial in perfect-field points. So they are not linear fibre functors acted on by pi_1.
errors: No mathematical error is visible. The text is a sketch with heavy hesitation (crossed-out passages about conjugation by automorphisms of k).

One point is plausible but not stated precisely: that the p-adic fibre depends only on the perfect closure. This holds for crystalline/Dieudonné invariants (W(k^perf) is the natural coefficient ring). It is not a statement about xi_{x,p} for arbitrary residue fields without passing to perfection.

The claimed rigidity of isomorphisms between fibres at different k-points is left unclear. Over non-algebraically-closed perfect k, Frobenius-conjugate points give fibres related only semilinearly. Grothendieck himself seems to notice this is a problem ('il faut mettre deux conjugués').

ideas.what: l-adic realizations of a motive over X form a local system: fibres at geometric points, canonical up to the pi_1(X) action (fundamental groupoid).
ideas.modern_name: l-adic local systems / étale fibre functors at geometric points

ideas.what: The p-adic realization at p = char is attached to points with values in perfect fields. It depends only on the perfect closure and takes values in W(k)-modules with F, V, FV = p. pi_1(X) does not act; automorphisms of k act semilinearly instead.
ideas.modern_name: Dieudonné modules / F-crystals as the crystalline realization; semilinear fibre functors (F-isocrystals) in Tannakian motive theory
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (crystals, 1966-68; Barsotti-Tate groups, 1970), Berthelot, Mazur; the Tannakian treatment is due to Saavedra Rivano (1972) and Deligne-Milne (1982)
ideas.where_published: Closest: 'Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes' (Dix exposés, 1968) and 'Groupes de Barsotti-Tate et cristaux' (ICM 1970). No published text uses this exact fibre-functor formulation at perfect points.

ideas.what: The asymmetry between l-adic and p-adic fibre data: pi_1 action versus a semilinear Aut(k/k(x)) action plus Frobenius structure.
ideas.modern_name: Failure of the crystalline realization to be a Q_p-linear fibre functor; Frobenius-semilinear (sigma-) structures
ideas.usually_credited_to: Saavedra Rivano, Deligne, Ogus (crystalline/F-isocrystal Tannakian categories)

missed.claim: This is an early (1965, before Grothendieck's published crystal theory) explicit formulation of the p-adic realization of motives over a base. It is attached to perfect-field-valued points, with the semilinear Aut(k) action replacing pi_1 and with F, V, FV = p as extra structure. It documents that the 'semilinear p-adic fibre functor' issue later treated by Saavedra Rivano and Deligne was already in Grothendieck's motivic Galois program in 1965.
missed.quote: Le groupe π1(X) n'opère plus sur ξ*_p, par contre le groupe des autom. de k sur k(x) opère sur ξ^{(x)}_p ... structure supplémentaire, les opérat. FV = p
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is historical priority and context for the crystalline side of Tannakian motive theory. It is not a new mathematical result.

deep.surprise_reason: The content (Dieudonné/crystalline realizations over W(k) with semilinear automorphisms and F, V) is standard today. The early date (1965) and its explicit framing within the motivic Galois theory over a base make it a modestly notable historical detail.
transcription_corrections: Line 2 likely reads 'dépendant du choix [du pt géom.] (π1(X) opère sur ξ_l)', with π1(X) the fundamental group, not 'dépendance du [?]'.
'Les ξ*_p dépendent du choix d'un pt de X à valeurs dans un corps V parfait, sans plus': 'corps' is crossed out and replaced by 'pt de X'.
'partie entière' refers to the W_p(k)-lattice (Witt vectors), i.e. the integral structure.
The left-margin vertical note seems to end '... En revanche, on a comme structure supplémentaire les opérat. F, V avec FV = p'.
The bottom-left note likely reads 'Il faut mettre deux conjugués à notation' or similar, i.e. a reminder about Frobenius-conjugates in the notation; the reading is uncertain.
